description: GeoVibe is a Melbourne-based team passionate about Earth observation, geospatial science, and environmental analytics. For NASA Space Apps 2026, we aim to develop an interactive tool to detect and visualise statistically significant Earth system trends using NASA data. We welcome teammates with skills in GIS, remote sensing, Python, statistics, data visualisation, and web development. Join us to explore our changing planet!
summary:
GeoVibe Agriculture is an interactive geospatial platform designed to make satellite-based agricultural monitoring more accessible. It brings together Sentinel-2 and Landsat 8/9 satellite imagery with NASA POWER precipitation data to help users explore vegetation conditions, moisture patterns, and environmental changes.

Users can select an agricultural field on an interactive map, choose a study period, and examine three vegetation indices: NDVI, NDMI, and EVI. The platform also provides historical trends, precipitation visualisations, satellite imagery, and vegetation change detection.

GeoVibe combines these datasets into one interface using Google Earth Engine, Python, FastAPI, and Mapbox. Its experimental Crop Condition Score compares recent vegetation observations against historical conditions.

The project aims to make Earth observation information easier to interpret for farmers, researchers, students, and agricultural decision-makers. Rather than predicting crop yields or diagnosing crop health, GeoVibe provides an accessible tool for exploring satellite-derived evidence and identifying areas that may require further investigation.
details:
How GeoVibe works

GeoVibe Agriculture is a web-based application that combines multispectral satellite imagery and climate information for field-level agricultural monitoring.

Users draw a polygon around a field and select a date range. The backend retrieves Sentinel-2 and Landsat 8/9 observations through Google Earth Engine, applies cloud and quality masks, and calculates three spectral indices:

  • NDVI: Describes vegetation greenness using red and near-infrared reflectance.
  • NDMI: Provides an indication of vegetation moisture conditions using near-infrared and shortwave infrared reflectance.
  • EVI: Measures vegetation greenness while reducing certain atmospheric and background influences.

The application displays satellite imagery, temporal observations, seasonal or monthly summaries, historical comparisons, and NDVI-based change detection. It also retrieves precipitation data from NASA POWER to provide environmental context.

Innovation and benefits

GeoVibe integrates satellite observations, vegetation indices, rainfall, and historical comparisons within a single interactive workflow.

An experimental Crop Condition Score compares recent NDVI, NDMI, and EVI values with earlier observations from corresponding periods. The score is intended as a descriptive indicator, not a validated measure of crop health.

The platform allows users to investigate fields without writing geospatial code or processing satellite imagery manually.

Technology and datasets

The application was developed with Python, FastAPI, Google Earth Engine, JavaScript, HTML, CSS, and Mapbox. Scientific calculations use Python libraries including SciPy.

Satellite imagery comes from Copernicus Sentinel-2 and Landsat 8/9, while NASA POWER provides precipitation data.

Intended impact and limitations

GeoVibe aims to support accessible agricultural monitoring, environmental education, and exploratory research. Potential applications include investigating vegetation trends, changes between periods, and possible relationships between rainfall and vegetation conditions.

Cloud cover, differences between satellite sensors, data availability, and the absence of field-based validation limit interpretation. Satellite-derived indicators should therefore not be treated as direct measurements of crop yield or definitive diagnoses of agricultural stress.
